blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Coquitlam total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Scott Creek Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Lasalle Place is the pocket's named townhouse street, shown on the City's trail guide beside the Hoy Creek and Town Centre Park trails, east of the Lansdowne Drive school campus.

blocks.text: Scott Creek Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: The named townhouse project here is the 42-unit complex at 1251–1271 Lasalle Place, recorded in City of Coquitlam Design Committee minutes of July 12, 1988 reviewing a roofing-material change for that project — a late-1980s strata, not a new build.

No apartment-condo building inside the Scott Creek pocket is named in a municipal, School District No. 43 (SD43) or BC Assessment public source; the attached stock found is townhouse-form strata only.

blocks.text: Scott Creek Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: City-wide zoning, Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) and Interim Official Community Plan (OCP) Bylaw No. 5511, 2026 detail is covered in full in the Scott Creek Coquitlam houses-for-sale guide and the Coquitlam condos-for-sale guide.

blocks.text: Scott Creek Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Scott Creek's own drainage is actively maintained at the townhouse edge: the City's instream-works list names Scott Creek at Runnel Drive (box culvert clean and inspect), Scott Creek at Lansdowne Drive (box culvert) and Scott Creek at Eagleridge Drive (box culvert) as work sites.

Eagle Ridge Outdoor Pool, an eight-lane 25-metre outdoor pool at Eagle Ridge Park, is seasonal — its listed 2026 season ran May 30 to September 7 — so a townhouse buyer does not get year-round swimming at that facility.

The Coquitlam Crunch Trail starts at Eagle Ridge Park on Runnel Drive and climbs 2.2 kilometres with 894 steps to Westwood Plateau, which is the trail access the Lasalle Place and Lansdowne townhouses share with the houses.

blocks.text: Scott Creek Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: One cost is strata-specific to this page: no municipal page states strata fees for the Lasalle Place complex, so the fee, contingency reserve fund balance and any special levy history come only from the unit's Form B and strata documents.

blocks.text: Scott Creek Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Route 185 is the pocket's bus spine, running Lansdowne Drive from Coquitlam Central Station to Panorama Drive and continuing as the 184 to Moody Centre Station.

blocks.text: Scott Creek Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the strata's own documents for the 1988-era Lasalle Place complex — depreciation report, envelope and roof history — because no municipal page publishes the building's condition.

blocks.text: Scott Creek home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

9 townhomes sold in Scott Creek with a median price of $1,049,900 (the middle half sold between $999,900 and $1,090,000), taking a median of 2 days to sell at 100.0% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $696 per square foot, a median year built of 2026 and a median strata fee of $424 a month.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Scott Creek?

faq.q: How old is the Lasalle Place townhouse complex?
